Based on my analysis of the test image and comparison with references:

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean leaf with a large, dark brown-to-black necrotic lesion
- Prominent yellowish-green halo surrounding the dark necrotic area
- Multiple holes where dead tissue has fallen out, giving a ragged appearance
- Some angular/vein-limited characteristics to the lesion edges

**Key differentiators:**
- The yellowish-green halo is a hallmark of Bacterial Blight
- Dead tissue falling out creating a ragged leaf appearance is the classic Bacterial Blight diagnostic feature
- Cercospora shows purple/bronze interveinal discoloration (not matching)
- Soybean Vein Necrosis shows lesions specifically along veins (test image has a larger consolidated lesion)
- Bacterial Pustule shows small raised bumps (not matching)
- Phyllosticta shows tan lesions with purplish margins in lower canopy (not matching the dark black center)
